concept: Sheet is the lid of an appliance opened to show every control of one device at once, rising from the bottom edge of a phone and standing as its own unit at the lower end of a wide screen.
family_difference: Dialog asks one question and waits for an answer, so the scrim does nothing and its keys close it. Sheet holds a device's full controls that act at once, so it has a close key in its header, closes on a scrim click, slides from its own edge instead of rising a few pixels, and can be dragged down by its printed bar when docked.

default_to_avoid.pattern: iOS style bottom sheet with a grey pill handle and a white rounded top
default_to_avoid.why_not: A grey pill is a second edge language and a white top is the surface NEVER rule in FORM.md; the handle here is printed ink with square ends.

default_to_avoid.pattern: side sheet drawer glued flush to the edge of the window (Material navigation drawer)
default_to_avoid.why_not: A rail fused to the window edge is no longer a unit of its own, and P6 caps panels so they do not become walls.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): a lid that opens to show the full control panel, then closes over it
Braun TP 1 radio-phonograph (Dieter Rams, 1959): the full set of controls on one face, read top to bottom
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, Dialog (Modal) pattern: focus moves in, Escape closes, focus returns to the opener

derivation.consequence: sits where the hand expects it (lower or right of the display)
derivation.form: On a phone the sheet rises from the bottom edge under the thumb; on a wide screen it stands at the lower inline end, inset from both edges.

derivation.consequence: capped so large panels do not swell into pillows
derivation.form: The radius is corner.panel, the cap, and the docked bottom corners are square because they meet the screen edge.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The device name, the lowercase model name and the close key share one header row on the top inset line.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: Dragging the printed bar is never the only way out: the close key, Escape and a click on the scrim close it too.

derivation.consequence: no entry choreography, no idle animation; transitions only on state
derivation.form: The body slides in from its edge as one piece on the enter easing and leaves faster on the exit easing; nothing inside it moves on its own.

options.name: lid, docked to the bottom on a phone and a unit at the lower end on wide screens
remote, a floating unit sized to its content on every screen
faceplate, the whole phone screen and a drawer flush with the edge on wide screens

variants.reason: A gives a phone the full width a fader needs and keeps the sheet a unit of its own on a laptop near the lower end where the hand is (P1); B wastes phone width and reads as Dialog's twin, and C hides the room it came from and glues a rail to the window edge (P6).

root.why: The sheet is a body of matte plastic with the capped panel radius and one light from the top left.

bottom.why: Docked to the bottom edge across the full width, the controls sit under the thumb on a phone held upright.

auto.why: The placement follows the screen, so a tall screen gets the docked sheet and a wide one the standing unit.

inline.why: A non-modal sheet sits in the flow of the page at a fixed place and covers nothing.

handle.why: The drag bar is printed in full ink on the plastic with square ends, flat like any printing on the case.

head.why: Device name, model name and close key share the top inset line, so the header is printing on the case.

title.why: The device name is printed at the title size in medium weight, so it is the first thing read.

model.why: The model name is printed lowercase at caption size in the secondary ink, like printing on a case.

content.why: Display, faders and rows sit on the same inset line as the header, never floating mid-surface.

actions.why: Optional keys sit together at the bottom and inline end, where the hand expects the main key.

data-state=open.why: The open sheet slides in from its edge on the enter easing, as one body with all its parts.

data-dragging=true.why: While the bar is held the body follows the finger directly, with no easing that would lag behind it.

@media orientation: portrait.why: On a screen taller than it is wide the sheet docks to the bottom edge, where the thumb is.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduced motion the sheet appears and leaves at once, with no slide and no fade.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the sheet keeps a real border and the bar takes the text colour, so both survive.

opacity.why: The body fades with its slide so the scrim and the sheet arrive and leave as one change of state.

transform.why: The only travel is the slide from the sheet's own edge over motion.release in and the shorter motion.exit out.
